newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lufthansa French 96 export air cargo revenues up 13 pct.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa French 96 export air cargo revenues up 13 pct.

text.p: The French unit of Lufthansa Cargo AG (LHAG) said net revenues from exports totalled 160 million francs in 1996, an increase of 13 percent on 1995.
LHAG France figures also showed the volume of export traffic shipped by LHAG France last year climbing by 28 percent to 17,600 tonnes, representing 54,500 air way bills, up 20 percent on 1995.

"1996 was an excellent performance for LHAG France and was largely down to favourable economic conditions which stimulated air cargo activity generally, the competitiveness of our rates, and the development of our provincial stations including Orly and Bordeaux " it said.
"Chartering a Boeing 747F from Paris to Atlanta on behalf of the French Olympic equestrian team, also boosted revenues and tonnage," a LHAG official told Reuters.

"So far 1997, has not been exceptional with tonnage in the first few months of the year being more or less stable on the same period last year. The current National Assembly elections -- with the final round on June 1 -- traditionally tends to put the country's industrial sector on hold and this is reflected in market conditions," the official said'
"We'll probably not have a idea on the underlying market trend before the end of June," he added.
Around 90 percent of LHAG France freight is trucked to Frankfurt with three to four services on a daily basis.
